description: Structured eval definitions for the VPC Peering Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across peering topologies (same-account same-region with DNS resolution and SG cross-ref, cross-account same-region with CIDR-based SG rules, inter-region peering for DR, IPv6 dual-stack peering, CIDR overlap prerequisite failure). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: Same-account same-region VPC peering with DNS resolution and SG cross-reference
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — same-account same-region peering, DNS resolution both sides, SG cross-VPC reference (same acct+region), both-sides route tables
eval_cases.prompt: Create a VPC peering connection between VPC vpc-aaa11122 (10.0.0.0/16) and VPC vpc-bbb22233 (10.1.0.0/16) in us-east-1. Same account 123456789012. Enable DNS resolution across the peered VPCs. Requester route table rtb-app111. Accepter route table rtb-data222. Security group sg-app should reference sg-data from the accepter VPC for port 443. Tags: Environment=production, Topology=app-to-data.
eval_cases.expected_output:
VPC_PEERING: vpc-aaa11122 ↔ vpc-bbb22233 (pcx-111222333)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Requester VPC: vpc-aaa11122 (10.0.0.0/16)
  [✓] Accepter VPC: vpc-bbb22233 (10.1.0.0/16)
  [✓] CIDR overlap check: PASS
  [✓] Account topology: Same-account (123456789012)
  [✓] Region topology: Same-region (us-east-1)
  [✓] Route table (requester): rtb-app111 → 10.1.0.0/16 via pcx
  [✓] Route table (accepter): rtb-data222 → 10.0.0.0/16 via pcx
  [✓] DNS resolution: AllowDnsResolutionFromPeeredVpc=true (both sides)
  [✓] Security group: cross-VPC reference (sg-app → sg-data)
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --vpc-peering-connection-ids pcx-111222333 --region us-east-1

eval_cases.name: Cross-account same-region VPC peering with CIDR-based SG rules
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — cross-account same-region peering, accepter account must accept, CIDR-based SG rules (SG cross-ref not supported cross-account)
eval_cases.prompt: Create a VPC peering connection between VPC vpc-prod111 (10.0.0.0/16) in account 123456789012 and VPC vpc-dev222 (10.2.0.0/16) in account 999999999999. Same region us-east-1. Requester route table rtb-prod-rt. Accepter route table rtb-dev-rt. No DNS resolution needed. Security group rules should use CIDR (cross-account). Tags: Environment=prod-to-dev.
eval_cases.expected_output:
VPC_PEERING: vpc-prod111 ↔ vpc-dev222 (pcx-222333444)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Requester VPC: vpc-prod111 (10.0.0.0/16)
  [✓] Accepter VPC: vpc-dev222 (10.2.0.0/16)
  [✓] CIDR overlap check: PASS
  [✓] Account topology: Cross-account (requester 123456789012, accepter 999999999999)
  [✓] Region topology: Same-region (us-east-1)
  [✓] Route table (requester): rtb-prod-rt → 10.2.0.0/16 via pcx
  [✓] Route table (accepter): rtb-dev-rt → 10.0.0.0/16 via pcx
  [✓] Security group: CIDR-based (cross-account — SG cross-ref not supported)

eval_cases.name: Inter-region VPC peering for DR replication with DNS resolution
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — inter-region peering (us-east-1 to us-west-2), peer-region specified, cross-region data transfer cost noted, DNS resolution enabled
eval_cases.prompt: Create a VPC peering connection between VPC vpc-useast111 (172.16.0.0/16) in us-east-1 account 123456789012 and VPC vpc-uswest222 (172.17.0.0/16) in us-west-2 account 123456789012. This is for cross-region DR replication. Enable DNS resolution. Requester route table rtb-useast-rt. Accepter route table rtb-uswest-rt. Tags: Environment=dr, Topology=useast-to-uswest.
eval_cases.expected_output:
VPC_PEERING: vpc-useast111 ↔ vpc-uswest222 (pcx-333444555)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Requester VPC: vpc-useast111 (172.16.0.0/16)
  [✓] Accepter VPC: vpc-uswest222 (172.17.0.0/16)
  [✓] CIDR overlap check: PASS
  [✓] Account topology: Same-account (123456789012)
  [✓] Region topology: Inter-region (requester us-east-1, accepter us-west-2)
  [✓] DNS resolution: AllowDnsResolutionFromPeeredVpc=true (both sides)
  [✓] Security group: CIDR-based (inter-region — SG cross-ref not supported)

eval_cases.name: Dual-stack IPv4+IPv6 VPC peering
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — dual-stack peering with IPv4 and IPv6 routes on both sides, IPv6 CIDRs cited
eval_cases.prompt: Create a VPC peering connection between VPC vpc-app-v6 (10.10.0.0/16, IPv6 2600:1f18:4113:a100::/56) and VPC vpc-data-v6 (10.11.0.0/16, IPv6 2600:1f18:4113:b200::/56) in us-east-1, account 123456789012. Both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic needed. Requester route table rtb-app-v6. Accepter route table rtb-data-v6. Tags: Environment=production, Protocol=dualstack.
eval_cases.expected_output:
VPC_PEERING: vpc-app-v6 ↔ vpc-data-v6 (pcx-444555666)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Requester VPC: vpc-app-v6 (10.10.0.0/16, IPv6 2600:1f18:4113:a100::/56)
  [✓] Accepter VPC: vpc-data-v6 (10.11.0.0/16, IPv6 2600:1f18:4113:b200::/56)
  [✓] CIDR overlap check: PASS
  [✓] Route table (requester): rtb-app-v6 → IPv4 + IPv6 routes
  [✓] Route table (accepter): rtb-data-v6 → IPv4 + IPv6 routes
  [✓] IPv6 routing: enabled (routes added both sides)

eval_cases.name: VPC peering with overlapping CIDR blocks (prerequisite failure)
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — both VPCs use 10.0.0.0/16; overlapping CIDRs break routing
eval_cases.prompt: Create a VPC peering connection between VPC vpc-alpha (10.0.0.0/16) and VPC vpc-beta (10.0.0.0/16) in us-east-1. Both in account 123456789012. The VPCs use the same CIDR block. Route tables rtb-alpha and rtb-beta.
eval_cases.expected_output:
VPC_PEERING: vpc-alpha ↔ vpc-beta
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] CIDR overlap check: FAIL — both VPCs use 10.0.0.0/16; overlapping CIDRs cause ambiguous routing
